blogs.title: Redo TAVI After Endocarditis: When to Re‑Enter the Valve
blogs.description: This post examines the clinical decision‑making process for performing a third TAVI in a patient who has recovered from prosthetic valve endocarditis. We’ll review guideline recommendations, the importance of confirming infection resolution with serial cultures and imaging, and the risk‑benefit balance of surgical versus transcatheter options in the era of high‑risk, elderly patients.

blogs.title: Valve‑within‑a‑Valve Chaos: Preventing Coronary Obstruction and Patient‑Prosthesis Mismatch
blogs.description: A deep dive into the technical nuances of TAV‑in‑TAV‑in‑TAV. We’ll cover how frame layering, high implantation, commissural alignment, and selective balloon pre‑ and post‑dilation can preserve coronary perfusion and optimize effective orifice area, especially when the anatomy has been altered by two prior transcatheter prostheses.

blogs.title: CT‑Guided Masterplan: Imaging the Unthinkable in Triple‑Valve Interventions
blogs.description: Discover how multidetector CT drives procedural planning for complex valve layering trials. The piece outlines step‑by‑step imaging workflows: annular sizing, minimal lumen measurement, coronary ostial height assessment, and 3‑D modeling to anticipate valve‑to‑coronary distances and frame interaction—critical for selecting the right prosthesis and deployment strategy.

blogs.title: Endocarditis‑Induced Bioprosthetic Degeneration: Pathophysiology and Prevention
blogs.description: Explore how bacterial infection accelerates structural valve deterioration beyond the usual wear‑and‑tear mechanisms. We’ll discuss evidence of leaflet fibrosis, bacterial embedding, and mechanical restriction after endocarditis, plus how prompt, targeted antibiotic therapy and careful imaging help differentiate “infection‑related” degeneration from classic SVD.

blogs.title: From First Valve to Lifetime Management: Surveillance and Reintervention in the TAVI Era
blogs.description: A forward‑looking post outlining how clinicians should plan for the long haul when a patient receives their first TAVI. Topics include surveillance intervals, imaging markers of impending failure, the role of computational modeling in predicting valve longevity, and strategies—such as valve‑fracture or leaflet‑laceration—reserved for future re‑interventions when multiple transcatheter valves are already in place.
